title: Extending the fundamental limit of atomic clock stability
summary: Optical atomic clocks have been rapidly developing in recent decades, resulting in major improvements in both precision and accuracy. As a result, they have become instrumental in multiple areas of applied and fundamental research. Despite all atomic frequency references having more than two energy-levels, the commonly used model for evaluating their ultimate limits assumes a two-level atom. This leads to frequency interrogation protocols and theoretical stability bounds that are suboptimal for a true multi-level atom.
